## My idea

Writing songs using ChatGPT

## What I aim to achieve

The idea that creativity is being 'killed' by AI is prevalent across my campus. The goal is to not only ask AI to write you a song based on your ideas - but it will also be translated. Hopefully we can connect ChatGPT to a music making app in order to not only write - but compose music. The music can be something inspirational like a Scottish ballad or alternatively, the students can use themselves as their own personal muses.

## Where the inspiration comes from

When asked to 'play with AI' our Dean of Science decided to jump into a tool and write a song then translate it.  He was surprised at how well the song translated into his local dialect.

## AI supporting student academic writing in higher education

## Author:

Ita Kennelly, Roisin Donnelly

## Contact details:

Ita.Kennelly@ncirl.ie, roisin.donnelly@tudublin.ie

## Role:

Lecturer, Head of School need to explore and potentially reconceptualise aspects of teaching, support and assessment in HE. We see writing as a key process in student learning which should not be diminished by recent developments and concerns.

## Institution/organisation:

National College of Ireland, Technological University Dublin

## Context:

Recent and continuing developments in AI mean that we

## Our idea

In light of AI, we are developing a 5 stage writing and inquiry model that will help lecturers to support student  academic  writing  and critical  inquiry  across  multiple disciplines in higher education.

## What we are aiming to achieve

We want to explore ways to sustain the role of writing in learning and assessments. We aim to support academic  staff  to  ensure  the continuation of student writing and inquiry by providing a model

![Image](data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAABcAAAAWCAIAAACkFJBSAAAAhElEQVR4nO2USwqEMBBEU6JBLzmu50Su9YDu/LWLGjQiRlowOsu8XUPl0TSkMHateU16HAA8UJD0LIMIGaYATJ5lmwVAP8mnqgeR+xuRLKxtvuV5l34Ks+h3cZjbuHBi/kESLSrRohMtOt6f5spFUmHPe5bC2qDedC21PDm29zjPzxrzBxs3NtZWORbEAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC)

## Tool(s) used:

Canva, A series of experiential practical strategies to positively utilise AI tools in a writing lab for academic staff so that they can in turn replicate with their own students for assignment writing.

to help redesign of teaching, learning and assessment approaches.

## Where the inspiration comes from

Richardson  (2005)  observes  that 'styles of writing are neither fixed nor neutral, but rather reflect the historically shifting domination of particular schools or  paradigms'  (p.960).  We  see  this as  another  shifting  paradigm  which challenges us to adapt and potentially raise the bar in teaching, writing and assessment practices. Richardson also promotes the idea of writing as thinking and this idea is central to our model.

## AI to generate a rt-based feedback

## Authors:

## Institution/organisation:

Daniela Casiraghi, Paola Corti, Bianca Santolini

## Contact details:

daniela.casiraghi@polimi.it paola.corti@polimi.it, bianca.santolini@polimi.it

## Role:

Educators

## Our idea

Provide  peer-to-peer  feedback  using AI-generated art-based content to stimulate peer/group discussion and reflection.

## What we are aiming to achieve

A deep and open discussion on the results achieved by individuals/groups, and on the path followed during a learning experience, enriching  the  feedback  with  AI-based images. Providing peer-to-peer feedback can be challenging and emotionally demanding. Art can support this activity mediating it through tools that focus on the message in a creative way.

Steps:

- Participants  and  facilitators  create  a negotiated rubric (we suggest to use iRubric

![Image](data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAABYAAAAWCAIAAABL1vtsAAAAgUlEQVR4nO2USwqAMAxEO6JFL6lrT+RaD+jOX1yMVKFRELS67VsVmjySQgfz0Jt/pP4E4EM/SVVMImRYP2DyLHMKAOMiZdNOIu9nIVlY29XVZYpxCVPcvMVByCKuODG/SaLCExVKVCj6U7lzunrA16uisDYo/o7IcS0+fud1/RZ8G+OmNta5PFYJAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC)

Politecnico di Milano

## Context:

Participants in an online/in presence/hybrid course of all levels.

## Tool(s) used:

ChatGPT, DALL·E 2, i-Rubric as a tool) at the beginning of the learning activity (a course, a lesson, …)

- Each participant/group of participants is assigned/choose/pick an output created by another participant/group of participants.
- They carefully look at the output and the rubric.
- They  formulate  their  version  of  the feedback for the selected output.
- Then, they ask ChatGPT to create prompts to be used with DALL·E to generate images to accompany the text version.
- The final feedback will include the initial text, the prompt (as a description of the image) the AI generated image.
- Open discussion in plenary on the outputs and on the effectiveness of this feedback strategy.

For a high-level output with something that can be improved: 'Dragon in a fantastic world, dark background'

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

For a high-level output that does not need any change: 'eagle flying in a clear blue mountain sky with open wings'

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

For more information on Idea 97: Art-based feedback toolkit.

## Recreando el pasado con IA

## My idea

## What I aim to achieve

Con base en la IA , crear  imágenes que  recreen  la  vida  cotidiana  y  la educación en la época del porfiriato.

En la clase de Historia de la Educación y la Pedagogía 4, de la Licenciatura en Pedagogía, abordamos en un primer  momento  el  contexto de la época a revisar, para posteriormente especificar los elementos, acciones, proyectos y documentos realizados en  materia educativa, haciendo énfasis  en las personas impulsoras y operadoras  de  los  mismos.  Es  así que, con base en lo revisado en clase (fuentes primarias, presentaciones de PowerPoint expuestas por la docente y trabajo colaborativo entre pares), se solicita al alumnado que elaboren una imagen que refleje la vida cotidiana y la educación en la época del porfiriato, la coloquen en un Padlet y le asignen un título y una descripción.

Si  bien  en  durante  el  porfiriato  ya existía  la  fotografía  en  México,  me parece  que  es  un  ejercicio  que  se puede replicar  para  experimentar  y mostrar  escenarios  o  ideas  de  las que el alumnado no tiene un referente gráfico,  pero  sí  profundo,  sobre  el tema en el que se enmarcan.

![Image](data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAABQAAAAVCAIAAADJt1n/AAAAi0lEQVR4nO2UMQ7CMBAEdy07jsTH8x46Cp5BwSfSBRInuUOWEShSCh8FVabxFTvyufByHHoAJAkoDBDwZZrmZRWBEQ8gNqE7X663extCvflM8/fmYUoihsUfH5mky+9mvexIV5/e8Q/ZhjPmNxzyP2VfDlUVzdSbovqWY/Cn2JjKIH/g0mFpWX+ooReWDzItxCyq1wAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==)

A  veces  se  piensa  que  la  IA  es una  herramienta  que  sólo  puede utilizarse para la enseñanza de las ciencias naturales o las ingenierías, quedando las ciencias sociales y las humanidades al margen. Con esta actividad pretendo que mi alumnado se familiarice con el uso de la IA y pueda ir identificando posibles usos en el marco de nuestras disciplinas. Aunado a que identifiquen que para que la IA realice un trabajo adecuado es necesario que ellas y ellos como profesionales de la educación estén documentados y sepan sobre el tema para valorar de manera adecuada si lo que la IA generó es pertinente o no y realizar los ajustes correspondientes. De esta forma, con esta actividad puedo evaluar: aprendizajes sobre el  contexto  y  la  educación  en  el porfiriato,  creatividad,  expresión gráfica, uso de herramientas digitales, redacción y síntesis.

## Where the inspiration comes from

La inspiración provino de un colega de la Universidad de Leeds que nos compartió una presentación de Power Point  en  la  que  generó  todas  las imágenes de la misma con base en una herramienta de IA.

## ChatGPT-4 as a co-authoring tool for formative tasks

## My idea

Using  ChatGPT-4  as  a  co-authoring tool  to  generate  role-play  scenarios and support with formative assessment activities.

## What I aim to achieve

I  use  role-play  activities  quite  often in  my  pedagogical  approaches  as  it helps my students to think  critically about a complex subject matter and explore their problem solving skills and reflective thinking abilities from various perspectives. Role-play engages students in an experiential learning process where, participants familiarise themselves to the viewpoint of a character or interest group and enacts that role within a set of rules to carry out a task, solve a problem or understand dynamics. Engaging in the process of thinking, feeling, watching and doing during a role-play exercise can provide students an opportunity to apply what they have learned to unfamiliar contexts in a relatively safe but realistic manner (Vogel, 2019).

As role-play is not a standard curriculum element (Vogel, 2019), it may be time restraining for educators to search for detailed role-play scenarios that  are (i)  accessible (ii) open source and (iii) adaptable for re-purpose so that they can be utilised within a particular context suited to the curriculum requirements

![Image](data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAABIAAAAVCAIAAADEqSm4AAAAcklEQVR4nO2UIQ6AMAxF+5eNkXBxzoNDcAwEl8AtYWO0BObAdArDM9/0panoxxZWIgIAIiEttkTc88Gstm7NN64fxmleWueqt4WYmKVOA2Cu+6DUjHLuwa+9+LWPNVtCRFgu6jTvbOcb/ZuidEnKR1UpnFSsKVIn/IibAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC)

and learning outcomes. In this context, module tutors can utilise ChatGPT-4 to generate co-authored contents of a roleplay scenario with carefully cosntrcuted prompts that are consciously aligned to  learning  outcomes.  While  this initiative may be seen as a time-saving effort, it can also be considered as a continuous professional developmental opportunity for educators to familiarise themselves with generative AI tools like ChatGPT-4, determine their potential 'ethical' uses to facilitate teaching and learning and identify inherent limitations of such applications when working in collaboration with AI.

## Where the inspiration comes from

I used a role-play exercise recently on a HE6 module.The students found it quite engaging and effective to asses their problem-solving skills. Upon reflection on  their  performances,  the  students requested for more role-play excercises to be incorporated within the curriculum to enable them to be more confident in  skills  application  processes.    This prompted me to think  if  I  could  use ChatGPT as a co-author to produce roleplay scenarios to support my students' learning  experiences.  The  idea  was inspired  by  a  Padlet  of  resources  on ChatGPT in Education, curated by Dr Phil Anthony as part of Digitally Enhanced Education webinars.

## Metaphors/analogies for AI

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

## Author:

## My idea

Maha Bali

## Contact details:

bali@aucegypt.edu, @bali\_maha

## Role:

Educational Developer, Educator

## Institution/organisation:

American University in Cairo

## Context

Can work in any context, as a warm-up activity.

Invite students to think about metaphors for AI: 'When AI is working for us, it is like…' and 'When AI is working against us, it is like…'

## What I aim to achieve

Find analogies for AI that can help us discuss its impacts and also to make the discussion light/fun at first, while deepening our understanding of it at the same time.

## Where the inspiration comes from

My mom! She told me 'AI is like fast/junk food' and it was such a good metaphor!

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

The teacher could think of one of their own metaphors/analogies - I'll use my moms (feel free to use with attribution): AI as fast food - it is quick and tasty but not healthy; however, occasionally, it saves us!
